chapter: Larry Shields and the Dixieland Band
title: Mother's family string band and early jazz
summary: Harry's mother, who died at 94 in 1948, said her brothers' string band with a flute played by ear, mazurkas and ragtime, which Harry takes as early jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What type of music did your mother's folks play? Would it be with a good beat to it, like jazz, or was it a different style? What would you say?

Well, my mother, my mother died in 1948, and she was the youngest of four children, so I understand. And she was 94 when she died in 48, so therefore her brothers were much older than her. She said there's quite a few years between her and her youngest brother, her brother Tony, who played guitar. And she first married, she was 18. And she said her brothers got together and they played for her wedding. And she said they didn't read music at all.

They were fakers then, but they didn't use a clarinet. She said a fellow by the name of, she didn't say, yeah, she said P-Nots, not P-Nots, P-Nots. He played the flute with this string band. They had a bass and a violin, a mandolin, two guitars, and a flute.
Do you suppose it was anything like jazz?

And she said even though they played, well she said ragtime, or jazz, she said yeah they could play mazurkas and shottish. And she even said that the fellow played the flute, worked for the sanitation department, and drove a dump cart, you know. Yeah.
But she said he was a very fine musician.
He was a regular flute. Flute player. A regular flute player.
Uh huh. So therefore they were evidently playing jazz then, what we call jazz now. And she said they, none of her brothers could read music. Yeah. Neither could her mother.
